name: Response Status
sourceRefs: apiv/dzero lib/dzero/segments/21_response_status.rb (field-id-to-symbol dictionary, read directly) cross-confirmed against eduardonunesp/ncpdp-telecom-fmt-book docs/response.md's own worked Approved (AN=A, F3, 5F, 6F) and Rejected (AN=R, FA, FB, 4F) examples -- the heart of the adjudication result.
responseStatus's own value vocabulary (confirmed from response.md): A=Approved, C=Captured, D=Duplicate, E=Error, P=Paid, R=Rejected.

Deliberately NOT modeled this pass: UF/UH/FQ/UG (additional message information group), 7F (help desk phone number qualifier), MA (url) -- present in dzero's own dictionary but genuinely secondary for a first-phase B1 response.

rejectCount/rejectCode are modeled as ORDINARY scalar fields (last-occurrence-wins on parse), NOT a true repeating group -- dzero's own reference implementation (segments/concerns/parser.rb's Hash[elements.map{...}] construction) exhibits the exact same last-value-wins behavior for a segment with multiple same-ID field occurrences, so this is a real, sourced simplification matching the reference implementation's own behavior, not an invented gap. A claim rejected for more than one reason will only surface its LAST reject code this phase -- named, deferred.
